document_check.note: Lizio R, Lopez S, Babiloni C, et al. 'Resting state EEG rhythms in different stages of chronic kidney disease with mild cognitive impairment', Neurobiology of Aging 130 (2023) 70-79, doi:10.1016/j.neurobiolaging.2023.05.014. The first author and year match the citation, and the document compares CKD-MCI (stages 3-4 and haemodialysis), cerebrovascular MCI and healthy controls, as the review states.

cited_result: Decreased occipital rsEEG alpha 2-3 (high-frequency alpha) power density in each MCI group (CKDMCI-3&4 n=22, CKDMCI-H n=15, CVMCI n=18) compared with healthy controls (n=30). This comes from a group x band x ROI MANOVA (F = 3.9, p < 0.001) with Bonferroni-corrected Duncan post hoc tests; occipital alpha 1 did not differ from controls.
tool_reason: The cited result compares an EEG biomarker between diagnostic groups and controls at a single time point in a retrospective cross-sectional archive study.

domains.rationale: Eligibility rules are stated for each group: CKDMCI with GDS ≤10 and Hachinski ≤5, CVMCI in the sub-acute post-stroke phase, and HC free of chronic systemic, neurological and psychiatric disease. The archive selection rules (maximise N; minimise MMSE, age, sex and education differences) are also given. The CKD stage cut-offs are not stated in the methods but eGFR is tabulated.

signalling.question: Were the criteria for inclusion in the sample clearly defined?
signalling.quote: All CKDMCI patients were selected to have the GDS (15-item GDS; Brown and Schinka, 2005) score of ≤10, pointing to the absence of depression. Furthermore, these CKDMCI patients were selected to have low cerebrovascular risk as indicated by modified Hachinski ischemia scores ≤5

domains.domain: 2. Study subjects and setting described in detail
domains.rationale: Recruitment sources are named for each group (Bari OPLON trial, Rome 10-Hz rehabilitation trial, three consortium units for HC), with a flowchart and demographic table. Recruitment dates are not given.

signalling.question: Were the study subjects and the setting described in detail?
signalling.quote: The CKDMCI patients were serially enrolled in a randomized way at the Department of Emergency and Organ Transplantation of the Hospital of the University of Bari (Italy) during a local clinical trial of the project entitled “OPportunities for active and healthy LONgevity”

domains.rationale: The grouping exposures (CKD stage, haemodialysis status, cerebrovascular disease) rest on laboratory renal markers (eGFR 39.9 vs 5.9 ml/min) and on clinical stroke assessment including the NIH Stroke Scale.

signalling.question: Was the exposure measured in a valid and reliable way?
signalling.quote: In all CKDMCI patients (i.e., CKDMCI-3&4 and CKDMCI-H), the blood sampling was collected and analyzed to extract the levels of glomerular filtration rate ... In all CVMCI patients, clinical, neuropsychological, and rsEEG data were acquired in the sub-acute phase after stroke (about 1 month after the event)

domains.domain: 4. Objective, standard criteria for the condition
domains.rationale: The MCI diagnosis uses a study-specific rule (CDR < 1 plus a test battery) with no published MCI criteria named. The sentence stating the rule appears in the CKDMCI paragraph but refers to 'all CVMCI patients'. CDR < 1 admits CDR 0, and Table 3 shows only 60% (CKDMCI-3&4) and 40% (CKDMCI-H) with an abnormal CDR. Table 2 shows non-memory tests largely normal (verbal fluency 0% abnormal) despite the 'multi-domain' label. Control status was judged in a neurological examination.

signalling.question: Were objective, standard criteria used for measurement of the condition?
signalling.quote: The CDR < 1 and the scores of this battery grounded the diagnosis of multi-domain MCI in all CVMCI patients of the present study. ... Clinical Dementia Rating (CDR) 0.3 ± 0.1 SE (60%) 0.3 ± 0.1 SE (40%)

domains.rationale: Age, sex, education and MMSE are named as matching factors. The authors also identify differences in recording time, setting and equipment between groups as a limitation.

signalling.question: Were confounding factors identified?
signalling.quote: (2) the different calendar time, settings, and equipment used in the rsEEG recordings for the CDKMCI, CVMCI, and HC participants

domains.domain: 6. Strategies to deal with confounding stated
domains.rationale: Demographic matching by archive selection is stated. However, recording centre, calendar time and equipment coincide completely with group membership (CKDMCI from Bari, CVMCI from Rome, HC from Brescia, Genoa and Troina). The reference montage was not standardised. No design or analytic strategy addresses this, and the MANOVA has no covariates. This confounder bears directly on every between-group spectral comparison, including the cited alpha result.

signalling.question: Were strategies to deal with confounding factors stated?
signalling.quote: the HC participants were enrolled at the following clinical units of our national consortium: IRCCS San Giovanni di Dio Fatebenefratelli of Brescia, IRCCS AOU S Martino-IST of Genoa, and IRCCS Oasi Research Institute of Troina ... The linked earlobe reference electrode was preferred, but not mandatory

domains.rationale: Spectral power used a standard FFT (Welch) method with individually defined bands and normalisation. But acquisition was not harmonised across centres (reference optional, variable sampling rates and equipment). Artefact rejection was by visual inspection, with no statement of blinding to group, and no reliability data are given.

signalling.question: Were the outcomes measured in a valid and reliable way?
signalling.quote: Particular attention was paid to the removal of epochs affected by physiological (i.e., ocular/ blinking, muscular, and head movements) or non-physiological (i.e., sweat, bad contact between electrodes and scalp, etc.) artifacts based on the visual analysis by two experts of EEG signals (C.D.P., R.L., G.N., or S.L.).

domains.rationale: The analysis is a log-transformed repeated-measures (M)ANOVA with sphericity correction, Bonferroni-corrected post hoc tests and an outlier check. This is appropriate for a group comparison of this kind, although there was no covariate adjustment and groups were small (15 to 30).

signalling.question: Was appropriate statistical analysis used?
signalling.quote: Table 4 reports the Duncan planned post-hoc (p < 0.05 Bonferroni correction for 8 frequency bands × 5 ROI = 40, p < 0.05/40 = 0.00125), size effect by Cohen’s d

overall: High (JBI item 6 'No' under this review's rule)
overall_rationale: Item 6 is 'No', which by this review's rule makes the overall rating high. Recording centre, calendar time and EEG equipment differ completely between groups and the authors acknowledge this without any design or analytic strategy, so the MCI-versus-control alpha difference cannot be separated from centre effects. MCI diagnostic criteria (item 4) and outcome measurement harmonisation (item 7) are unclear.

applicability.concern: Non-AD MCI aetiologies with small groups
applicability.rationale: The groups are CKD-related MCI and sub-acute post-stroke MCI (15 to 22 per group) from Italian centres. Generalisation to AD-type MCI or community MCI is limited.
